questions.text: How many Rashidun (rightly-guided) caliphs ruled the first caliphate?
questions.explanation: The Rashidun Caliphate was ruled by four caliphs: Hazrat Abu Bakr, Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman and Hazrat Ali.

questions.text: For how many years did the Rashidun Caliphate last?
questions.explanation: The lesson says the Rashidun Caliphate lasted for 30 years.

questions.text: What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique?
questions.explanation: His name was Abdullah; Abu Bakr was his kuniyyat and Siddique was his title.

questions.text: Who was the first among men to accept Islam?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr was the first among men to accept Islam.

questions.text: Who was elected as the first caliph of Islam?
questions.explanation: After the death of Rasoolullah (PBUH), Hazrat Abu Bakr was elected as the first caliph.

questions.text: Which title was given to Hazrat Umar?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Umar was given the title 'Farooq', the one who distinguishes between right and wrong.

questions.text: For about how long did Hazrat Umar serve as caliph?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Umar served Islam and the Muslims as caliph for ten and a half years.

questions.text: Why was Hazrat Usman known as 'Ghani'?
questions.explanation: He was a rich trader who spent generously in the way of Allah, so he was called Ghani.

questions.text: What does 'Zun Noorain' mean?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Usman married two daughters of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), so he was called Zun Noorain, holder of two lights.

questions.text: Who was the first among children to accept Islam?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Ali was the first among children to accept Islam, at about ten years of age.

questions.text: Hazrat Ali is also known as:
questions.explanation: Because he was very courageous, Hazrat Ali is known as 'the Lion of Allah'.

questions.text: Which caliph was the third caliph of Islam?
questions.explanation: After the martyrdom of Hazrat Umar, Hazrat Usman became the third caliph.

questions.text: How many vowel letters are there in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The lesson says there are five vowels: a, e, i, o and u.

questions.text: A group of two letters that makes a single sound is called a:
questions.explanation: A digraph is a group of two letters that makes one sound, e.g. 'ch' in chick.

questions.text: Which of these is an uncountable noun?
questions.explanation: Uncountable nouns have no plural form, e.g. water, weather, furniture.

questions.text: In the word 'lamb', which letter is silent?
questions.explanation: In 'lamb' the letter b is written but not pronounced.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'Caterpillar' in Unit 2?
questions.explanation: The poem 'Caterpillar' in this unit is by Christina Rossetti.

questions.text: In the poem, how is the caterpillar described?
questions.explanation: The poem begins: 'Brown and furry, Caterpillar in a hurry'.

questions.text: Where is the caterpillar walking to in the poem?
options: To the shady leaf or stalk
questions.explanation: The poet asks the caterpillar to take its walk to the shady leaf or stalk.

questions.text: What will the caterpillar become?
questions.explanation: A caterpillar is a stage in the life cycle of a butterfly.

questions.text: The word 'hover' means:
options: to stay in the air in one place
questions.explanation: In the vocabulary list, hover means to stay in the air in one place.

questions.text: A 'stalk' is:
options: the main stem of a plant
questions.explanation: The vocabulary list gives stalk as the main stem of a plant.

questions.text: In which word is the letter 'w' silent?
questions.explanation: In 'wrap' the w is not pronounced.

questions.text: A word that refers to a group of people or things is called a:
questions.explanation: A collective noun refers to a group, e.g. a team of players, a herd of deer.

questions.text: Choose the correct collective noun: a ___ of flowers.
questions.explanation: We say a bouquet of flowers.

questions.text: Choose the correct article: She is ___ honest girl.
questions.explanation: The 'h' in honest is silent, so the word starts with a vowel sound and takes 'an'.

questions.text: In 'Shazia eats Australian apples', the word 'Australian' is an adjective of:
questions.explanation: An adjective of origin tells where something comes from, e.g. Chinese, Turkish, Australian.

questions.text: In Mahnoor's story, how did she make people care about plants and insects?
questions.explanation: Her mother suggested a colourful chart; Mahnoor and her friends made charts and put them up.

questions.text: In its raw form, chocolate comes from:
questions.explanation: The lesson says chocolate comes from cocoa trees in its raw form.

questions.text: Where do the flowers of a cocoa tree grow?
questions.explanation: Surprisingly, cocoa flowers grow on the trunk of the tree, not on its branches.

questions.text: How many beans does each cocoa pod contain?
questions.explanation: Each pod contains 20 to 40 beans.

questions.text: How long does a cocoa pod take to ripen?
questions.explanation: It takes the pod about six months to ripen.

questions.text: Who brought chocolate to Spain in the 1500s?
questions.explanation: Chocolate came from Central and South America to Spain through Spanish explorers.

questions.text: In ancient times, chocolate was a symbol of:
questions.explanation: Only the rich could afford it, so chocolate was a symbol of wealth.

questions.text: The edible pieces left after removing the shells of roasted beans are called:
questions.explanation: After the shells are removed, the remaining edible pieces are called nibs.

questions.text: What is added to the nib paste besides sugar?
questions.explanation: The nibs are mixed with sugar; dried milk and some flavours are then added.

questions.text: What should we always do after eating chocolate?
questions.explanation: The lesson reminds us to always brush our teeth after eating chocolate.

questions.text: A combination of two vowel sounds in a single syllable is called a:
questions.explanation: A diphthong begins with one vowel sound and moves to another, e.g. coil, pain, now.

questions.text: A pie chart is used to:
questions.explanation: The lesson says a pie chart compares parts of a whole, while a bar graph compares different groups.

questions.text: Words like 'first', 'then', 'next' and 'finally' are called:
questions.explanation: Joining (transition) words connect one sentence or paragraph to the next.

questions.text: Where did the class go on their historical trip?
questions.explanation: The children took the school bus for a trip to the Pakistan Army Museum, Lahore.

questions.text: Why did Tashif collect pictures about the Pakistan Army?
options: His uncle was an army officer
questions.explanation: It was his hobby, as his uncle was an army officer.

questions.text: How many Nishan-e-Haider heroes did the children want to meet in the museum?
questions.explanation: They waited to meet the eleven heroes from the armed forces who laid down their lives.

questions.text: What does 'Nishan-e-Haider' mean?
questions.explanation: The teacher told them Nishan-e-Haider means 'Mark of the Lion'.

questions.text: The Nishan-e-Haider is Pakistan's:
questions.explanation: It is the highest military award, given for an extraordinary act of bravery in which the soldier gives his life.

questions.text: What did the children see on entering the museum building?
questions.explanation: Inside the museum they saw four captured Indian tanks with a brief history.

questions.text: The 'Rebirth of the Nation' gallery showed the Quaid-e-Azam addressing the assembly on:
questions.explanation: It had a life-size portrait of the Quaid addressing the assembly of Pakistan on August 11, 1947.

questions.text: For about how long did the children explore the museum?
questions.explanation: The narrator explored the museum with classmates for more than three hours.

questions.text: Which word contains a diphthong?
questions.explanation: In 'play' the sound changes from one vowel to another in one syllable, so it is a diphthong.

questions.text: Why are soldiers called our national heroes?
options: They sacrifice their lives to guard the country
questions.explanation: The lesson describes heroes who laid down their lives to guard the sacred land of Pakistan.

questions.text: Which noun has the same form in singular and plural?
questions.explanation: Some nouns do not change in the plural, e.g. 'The sheep are grazing in the field.'

questions.text: Words with opposite meanings are called:
questions.explanation: Antonyms are words with opposite meanings; synonyms have similar meanings.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'Thank You, Lord'?
questions.explanation: The poem 'Thank You, Lord' is by Mary Fairchild.

questions.text: How does the poet start each day?
options: By taking a moment to bow and pray
questions.explanation: 'Lord, in the morning I start each day, by taking a moment to bow and pray.'

questions.text: What does the poet start her prayer with?
questions.explanation: 'I start with thanks, and then give praise for all your kind and loving ways.'

questions.text: What will the poet do when sunshine turns to rain?
questions.explanation: She says she won't doubt or hide in fear, because God is with her.

questions.text: Until when will the poet keep God close in sight?
options: Until she crawls into bed at night
questions.explanation: 'And I will keep you close in sight until I crawl in bed tonight.'

questions.text: A group of two or three consonants in a word, each keeping its sound, is called a:
questions.explanation: In a consonant cluster each consonant keeps its own sound, e.g. 'str' in street.

questions.text: In 'Getting Started', why is cutting trees wrong?
questions.explanation: The tree in the picture says, 'Please, don't kill me! I give you oxygen.'

questions.text: Which place did Mahira and Aqsa visit in the dialogue?
questions.explanation: Mahira asks Aqsa whether she enjoyed the visit to the Faisal Masjid.

questions.text: Words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings are called:
questions.explanation: Homophones sound alike but differ in meaning and spelling, e.g. sea/see.

questions.text: What is the feminine of 'king'?
questions.explanation: King is masculine; its feminine gender noun is queen.

questions.text: Where did Rehan find his friend Sa'ad sitting alone?
options: On a bench in a park
questions.explanation: One evening Rehan found Sa'ad sitting alone on a bench in a park.

questions.text: Why was Sa'ad upset?
options: He had been rude to a classmate
questions.explanation: Sa'ad was ashamed of being rude to a classmate who limped while walking.

questions.text: What was the name of the boy Sa'ad was rude to?
questions.explanation: Sa'ad made fun of Faraz, who limped while walking.

questions.text: Faraz had been selected in the team as a:
questions.explanation: Sa'ad, the captain, was shocked that Faraz had been selected as wicket keeper.

questions.text: What happened to Faraz because of Sa'ad's rude behaviour?
questions.explanation: Faraz was so depressed by the rude behaviour that he left school.

questions.text: What did Rehan advise Sa'ad to do?
options: Go to Faraz's house and say sorry
questions.explanation: Rehan said it was not too late and told Sa'ad to go and apologise.

questions.text: How did Faraz respond to Sa'ad's apology?
questions.explanation: Faraz was a good boy; he forgave Sa'ad and hugged him at once.

questions.text: What is the main lesson of 'Valuing Others'?
options: Treat differently-abled people with kindness and respect
questions.explanation: The story teaches that we must value others and never be rude to differently-abled people.

questions.text: Before a vowel sound, 'the' is pronounced as:
questions.explanation: 'The' is pronounced 'thee' before a vowel sound (the apple) and 'thuh' before a consonant sound.

questions.text: Which phrase is a polite way to seek permission?
questions.explanation: 'May I borrow ...?' politely asks permission before using someone else's things.

questions.text: Which languages are spoken in Punjab according to the lesson?
questions.explanation: The lesson says that in Punjab people speak Punjabi and Seraiki.

questions.text: Shina, Balti and Burushaski are regional languages of:
questions.explanation: In Gilgit-Baltistan, Shina, Balti and Burushaski are regional languages.

questions.text: The Sindhi cap and ajrak are part of the traditional dress of:
questions.explanation: The Sindhi cap and ajrak are part of men's dress in Sindh.

questions.text: Which festival in Balochistan attracts people from all across the country?
questions.explanation: In Balochistan, the Sibi Festival attracts people from all across the country.

questions.text: Hospitality, hard work and bravery are distinctive features of:
questions.explanation: Hospitality, hard work and bravery are features of Pakhtunwali, the Pakhtun way of life.

questions.text: Which is a prominent traditional dress of Kashmiri men and women?
questions.explanation: Phiran is a prominent traditional dress of Kashmiri men and women.

questions.text: Which festival is celebrated every year in Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The lesson says Pirchinasi is celebrated every year in Kashmir.

questions.text: Sindhi culture is dominated by great:
questions.explanation: Sindhi culture is dominated by great Sufis, mystics and martyrs.

questions.text: Poetry and storytelling are very popular among the:
questions.explanation: The lesson says poetry and storytelling are very popular among the Baloch.

questions.text: Pakhtun men often wear a turban or a:
questions.explanation: Pakhtun men usually wear shalwar kameez, a waistcoat and a turban or a pakol hat.

questions.text: In 'He is playing', the verb 'is' is used as a:
questions.explanation: When be, do or have are used with a main verb, they are helping verbs.

questions.text: In 'You are late', the verb 'are' is used as a:
questions.explanation: When be, do or have are used alone without another verb, they are main verbs.

questions.text: Who asked the children to make a poster about good study habits?
questions.explanation: Miss Hina told them to make a poster about good study habits.

questions.text: Where was the poster displayed?
questions.explanation: When the poster was completed, it was displayed in the classroom.

questions.text: Which of these is a good study habit from the poster?
questions.explanation: The poster lists: set your goals, make a timetable, make notes and revise classwork.

questions.text: What result did the narrator get after adopting good study habits?
questions.explanation: In the final term the narrator got first position in the class.

questions.text: To whom did the narrator write the invitation letter?
questions.explanation: The invitation begins 'Dear Asif' and is signed 'Your cousin'.

questions.text: When was the party arranged?
questions.explanation: The invitation says the party was on Friday evening at the narrator's house.

questions.text: In the dialogue, what had the son forgotten?
options: That he had a test tomorrow
questions.explanation: He had been playing for two hours and forgot he had a test the next day.

questions.text: What does Baba advise his son?
options: There is a time for play and a time for study
questions.explanation: Baba says there is a time for play and a time for study, and things should be done on time.

questions.text: Which pronoun shows possession?
questions.explanation: 'His' shows possession (his book); he, they and we are subject pronouns.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'Whole Duty of Children'?
questions.explanation: 'Whole Duty of Children' is by Robert Louis Stevenson.

questions.text: According to the poem, a child should always say:
questions.explanation: 'A child should always say what's true.'

questions.text: When should a child speak, according to the poem?
questions.explanation: 'And speak when he is spoken to.'

questions.text: Where should a child behave mannerly, according to the poem?
questions.explanation: 'And behave mannerly at table, at least as far as he is able.'

questions.text: The poem 'Whole Duty of Children' is mainly about:
questions.explanation: The poem talks about good manners a child should follow.

questions.text: Why did Mama ask Sidra to take a bath before breakfast?
options: To take care of personal hygiene
Because she was late for school
questions.explanation: Mama says, 'We should always take care of our personal hygiene.'

questions.text: In the word 'helped', the -ed ending sounds like:
questions.explanation: After p, k, sh, ch, s and f, the -ed ending sounds like 't' (helped, thanked).

questions.text: In the word 'wanted', the -ed ending sounds like:
questions.explanation: After t or d, the -ed ending is pronounced 'id' (wanted, needed).

questions.text: A table of contents helps us to:
questions.explanation: The table of contents helps us to find the chapters in a book.

questions.text: We should wash our hands with soap:
questions.explanation: The lesson reminds us to wash hands before and after a meal.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: We ___ speak rudely to our elders.
questions.explanation: We should not speak rudely to our elders; 'should not' shows something we must avoid.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: You ___ go to school on time.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is used for advice or duty: you should go to school on time.

questions.text: What did Sara bring home in 'Be Aware, Be Safe'?
questions.explanation: Mother asks Sara, 'Who gave you this doll?'

questions.text: Who gave Sara the doll?
questions.explanation: Sara says there was a man in the street who gave it.

questions.text: What did Mother say about accepting gifts from strangers?
options: It is fine if they smile
questions.explanation: Mother says it is not good to accept gifts from strangers because it might be dangerous.

questions.text: If a stranger offers you a ride, a toy or candy, you should:
questions.explanation: Mother says to say 'No!', walk away quickly and tell her or Baba.

questions.text: What did Sara and Ahsan promise their mother?
options: To share all their activities with her
questions.explanation: Sara promises, 'I will share all my activities with you.'

questions.text: Why should we not be friendly with strangers?
questions.explanation: Mother explains that it might be dangerous for children.

questions.text: Sara's brother in the lesson is named:
questions.explanation: Sara and her brother Ahsan entered their home.

questions.text: Past tense of regular verbs is formed by adding:
questions.explanation: Regular verbs form their past tense by adding -d or -ed, e.g. play-played.

questions.text: Adverbs of time tell us:
questions.explanation: Adverbs of time (today, yesterday, soon) tell us when an action happens.

questions.text: Which sentence is in the future tense?
questions.explanation: The future tense shows actions that will happen, using 'will'.

questions.text: How did the fox serve soup to the stork?
options: In a bowl with a lid
questions.explanation: The cunning fox served the soup in flat plates.

questions.text: Why could the stork not eat from the flat dish?
questions.explanation: The stork's beak was so long that he could not sip from the flat dish.

questions.text: How did the stork serve the meal to the fox?
options: In a jar with a narrow neck
questions.explanation: The stork served the meal in a jar with a narrow neck.

questions.text: What did the stork tell the fox at the end?
options: Do not ridicule or degrade anyone; Allah has made us all equal
questions.explanation: The stork said calmly, 'Do not ridicule or degrade anyone... Allah has made us all equal.'

questions.text: How did the story end?
options: The fox said sorry and they became friends
questions.explanation: The fox was ashamed, said sorry, and they became friends.

questions.text: What kind of animal was the fox in the story?
questions.explanation: The fox always teased others and played a trick on the stork.

questions.text: In which type of sentence does our voice rise at the end?
questions.explanation: In yes-no questions such as 'Do you obey traffic signs?' the voice rises at the end.

questions.text: In a wh-question like 'What is your name?' the voice usually:
questions.explanation: In wh-questions the voice falls on the final stressed syllable.

questions.text: The contraction of 'do not' is:
questions.explanation: An apostrophe replaces the missing letter: do not becomes don't.

questions.text: The contraction of 'I am' is:
questions.explanation: I am becomes I'm; the apostrophe stands for the missing 'a'.

questions.text: What did Ahsan's teacher give him?
questions.explanation: Ahsan's teacher gave him a brochure on traffic rules and road safety.

questions.text: What problem did Ahsan see in front of his school?
questions.explanation: Ahsan said there is always a traffic jam in front of his school.

questions.text: Why did people not follow traffic rules near Ahsan's school?
options: There was no traffic police on that road
questions.explanation: Ahsan never saw traffic police there, so nobody followed the rules.

questions.text: To whom did Ahsan write the letter?
questions.explanation: With his father's help, Ahsan wrote to the Inspector General, Traffic Police Headquarters, Islamabad.

questions.text: Where should we cross the road?
questions.explanation: The brochure says: cross only at the zebra crossing.

questions.text: What should we do before crossing the road?
options: Look to the left and right
questions.explanation: The brochure says look to your left and right before crossing the road.

questions.text: While riding a motorbike or bicycle, we should wear a:
questions.explanation: One of the brochure's rules is 'Wear a helmet'.

questions.text: In a car, we should always:
questions.explanation: The brochure says: fasten your seatbelt and sit quietly in the back seat.

questions.text: Ahsan's father said helping the police by reporting traffic issues is our:
questions.explanation: His father said, 'As a good citizen, it is our moral duty to help the police.'

questions.text: Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
questions.explanation: Past continuous = was/were + verb-ing, for actions in progress in the past.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'Little Things'?
questions.explanation: 'Little Things' is by Julia A. Carney.

questions.text: According to the poem, little drops of water make the:
questions.explanation: 'Little drops of water, little grains of sand, make the mighty ocean and the pleasant land.'

questions.text: Little grains of sand make the:
questions.explanation: The grains of sand make the pleasant land.

questions.text: What makes our earth an Eden, according to the poem?
options: Little deeds of kindness and little words of love
questions.explanation: 'Little deeds of kindness, little words of love, make our earth an Eden.'

questions.text: The main idea of 'Little Things' is that:
questions.explanation: The poem teaches that little things are not useless; everything has its importance.

questions.text: Little errors, according to the poem, lead the soul:
options: away from the path of virtue
questions.explanation: 'So the little errors lead the soul away from the path of virtue.'

questions.text: Using body parts and gestures to communicate feelings is called:
questions.explanation: Non-verbal communication uses body parts and gestures to show feelings and emotions.

questions.text: The rise and fall of the voice while speaking is called:
questions.explanation: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice while speaking.

questions.text: Which pair of words rhymes in the poem?
questions.explanation: 'Sand' and 'land' rhyme in the first stanza.
